docs.title: Lessons Learned KB
docs.text: Ad Hoc's human-governed, AI-curated knowledge base of project lessons learned. Every claim is traced to a source document. Only reviewer-approved pages appear here.

docs.title: What's in the KB
docs.text:
Section Status Purpose Retrospectives Empty — needs content One page per project — scope, outcomes, metrics, root causes Recommendations Empty — needs content Quantified claims indexed by capability area and lesson type Incident Reviews Empty — needs content Postmortem synthesis, root-cause findings, decision drivers Capability Areas Empty — needs content Cross-project synthesis by service line Best Practices Empty — needs content Canonical practice statements with evidence chains Client Context Empty — needs content Client/agency working patterns and relationship history Anti-Patterns Empty — needs content Documented failure patterns to recognize and avoid

This is a freshly bootstrapped KB — no source material has been synthesized yet. See the User Guide for how to contribute the first pages.

docs.title: How to read lifecycle and confidence badges
docs.text: Badge Meaning active Reviewer-approved. Ready to reuse. draft Not yet reviewed. Do not rely on without checking the source. stale Source material updated since last compile. Verify before use. contradicted Two sources conflict. Awaiting maintainer resolution. high confidence Metric present in source with clear provenance. medium confidence Single source, qualitative-only, or missing metadata. low confidence Do not rely on for decisions. Background context only.

docs.title: Sensitivity policy
docs.text:
Only public pages are meant for broad sharing. Internal analysis and restricted content (incident feedback, sensitive client detail) are never included in anything shared outside the KB maintainer group.

Maintained by the Ad Hoc delivery team. To contribute, see the User Guide or go to Admin to see how to add source material.

docs.title: Admin — Upload New Materials
docs.text:
Who this is for

KB maintainers only. There is currently no dedicated admin UI for this KB — content is added directly to the repo.

docs.title: Context folders
docs.text:
Select the folder that matches your content type:

Folder Use for Sensitivity Wiki destination Retrospectives Project completion notes, sprint retros, exit interviews Internal retrospectives/ Recommendations (raw) Unverified metrics, capture notes Internal recommendations/ Incident Reviews (raw) Postmortems, evaluator/stakeholder feedback Restricted Not published Anti-Patterns (raw) Documented failure patterns, near-misses Restricted Not published Engagement Notes Internal status notes, working docs Internal Not published Capability Areas Cross-project practice-area write-ups Public capability-areas/ Best Practices (raw) Draft practice statements Internal best-practices/

docs.title: How to add new material
docs.text:
1. Add the source .md file to the appropriate context/<folder>/ directory in the repo.
  2. Add an entry to that folder's manifest.yaml (path, as_of_date, content hash, sensitivity).
  3. Open a Claude Code session in the repo and run a KB synthesis session (see agent/agents.md and .claude/agents/kb-synthesis.md), or dispatch the KB Synthesis GitHub Action manually from the Actions tab (or gh workflow run kb-synthesis.yml -f folder=<folder> -f filename=<file>) if you want CI to do it.
  4. Review the resulting PR (or, for the CI path, the direct commit) before treating any page as active.
  5. Merging to main triggers the Build Wiki action, which rebuilds wiki/site/ and redeploys.

docs.title: Convert non-markdown files first
docs.text:
The KB only accepts .md files. For PDFs, Word documents, or PowerPoints:

pip install markitdown
markitdown your-file.pdf > output.md

Review the output for formatting artifacts before adding it to context/.

docs.title: Sensitivity rules
docs.text:
• Restricted material (incident feedback, sensitive personnel/client detail) must go into context/incident-reviews-raw/ or context/anti-patterns-raw/ — never into retrospectives or recommendations folders.
  • The synthesis agent enforces sensitivity downstream, but correct folder assignment is the first line of defense.
  • When in doubt, use a more restrictive folder.

docs.title: Start Here — KB Workflow
docs.text: This page maps the KB in the order you'll use it.

docs.title: The 4-step KB workflow
docs.text: 1. BEST PRACTICES  →  2. RECOMMENDATIONS  →  3. RETROSPECTIVES  →  4. REUSE

docs.title: Step 1 — Best Practices: Find the proven approach
docs.text:
Start here. Best practices tell you what has worked — canonical, evidence-backed practices the org has proven out.

Action: Read the Best Practices index. Which practice maps to the work you're about to start?

docs.title: Step 2 — Recommendations: Pull the evidence
docs.text:
Go to the Explore Recommendations page. Filter by:

  • Capability — matches the workstream you're planning
  • Lesson type — process / technical / people-org / client-relationship / tooling
  • Confidence: high — only rely on high confidence recommendations without caveats; medium with attribution

See the Recommendations index for the full capability list.

docs.title: Step 3 — Retrospectives: Anchor to a project
docs.text:
Recommendations are only as credible as the projects behind them. Map each recommendation to a retrospective record for context.

See the Retrospectives index once pages exist.

⚠️ Draft pages require reviewer approval before relying on them for planning. Check for the banner at the top of the page.

docs.title: Step 4 — Reuse correctly
docs.text:
Confidence How to use high Cite directly with the metric medium Cite with attribution ("as documented in…") or verify with the original team before relying on it low Do not rely on for planning decisions

Traceability: every recommendation links back to a context/ source file via footnotes. If someone asks for the source, follow the footnote to the context/ path in the repo.

docs.title: Also check
docs.text:
• Anti-Patterns — recognize a failure pattern before it repeats
  • Client Context — client-specific working history

Questions about a page? Check the User Guide. To contribute content, go to Admin.

docs.title: What this KB is for
docs.text: A small, high-confidence collection of pages that a delivery team can pull from when planning or steering an engagement: what happened on past projects, what recommendations follow from that, canonical best practices, failure patterns to watch for, and client-specific context.

docs.title: Adding new source material
docs.text:
1. Drop a markdown source file into the matching context/<folder>/ directory (see Admin for the folder list).
  2. Add a manifest entry.
  3. Run (or dispatch) a KB synthesis session. See agent/agents.md for the full session workflow and CLAUDE.md for the editorial rules the agent follows.
  4. Review the PR (or direct commit, for CI-triggered synthesis) before treating a page as reviewer-approved.

docs.title: Reading confidence and lifecycle
docs.text: See the badge legend on the Home page.
